title: Hierarchically Porous Unsubstituted Olefin‐Linked COF With Synergistically Enhanced Electronic and Ionic Conductivities for High‐Performance Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with synergistically enhanced ionic/electronic conductivities, improved active site utilization, and increased chemical stability for achieving high‐performance lithium–ion battery (LIB) cathodes remain a significant challenge. Here, we report the rational design of a novel unsubstituted olefin–linked, highly crystalline COF (namely HATN–ICTO COF) as a cathode for LIBs. The HATN–ICTO COF integrates extended fully conjugated π–networks, hierarchical porosity, and dual redox–active centers, enabling a synergistic improvement in ionic and electronic conductivity as well as a high theoretical capacity. This unique unsubstituted olefin linkage also endows the COF with excellent chemical stability, thereby ensuring long‐term cycling performance. Meanwhile, the hierarchical porous architecture of the COF can effectively buffer the volume expansion during repeated charge–discharge processes, mitigating electrode damage. The COF delivers a high specific capacity of 293 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 A g − 1 and maintains 206 mAh g − 1 at 10.0 A g − 1 , with outstanding cycling performance of 155 mAh g − 1 at 5.0 A g − 1 after 18,000 cycles. Additionally, a pouch cell based on the HATN–ICTO COF//Li configuration was also demonstrated. This work provides fundamental insights into structure–property relationships governing charge delocalization and redox activity in COFs.

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS 2 /Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS 2 /C nanospheres (HMMoS 2 /C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS 2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li + diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS 2 /C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g − 1 at 0.3 A g − 1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1 , and outstanding long‐term cycling stability. This work establishes coordination‐driven self‐assembly as a versatile route to helical mesoporous materials for energy storage.

title: Spin and Charge Engineering of a BiCuMn Nanoalloy Catalyst for Industrial‐Scale Electrosynthesis of Glycine
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic C–N coupling provides a sustainable route for α‐amino acids, yet its practicality is limited by poor selectivity and durability at industrially relevant current densities. Here, we report a Bi‐based nanoalloy catalyst with atomically dispersed Cu and Mn (BiCuMn@C) for industrial‐level glycine electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical results reveal that Cu modulates the electronic structure of Bi sites via d ‐ p hybridization, enhancing the adsorption/activation of nitrogen‐containing species, while spin‐polarized electrons from Mn are delivered to adjacent *NO intermediates, promoting their hydrogenation to *NHO on the pathway to NH 2 OH. This spin‐charge engineering disrupts the intrinsic scaling relationship between *NO and *NHO adsorption, enabling simultaneous enhancement of activity and selectivity. As a result, BiCuMn@C achieves a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 78.9% at a current density of 533.1 mA cm −2 , corresponding to a yield rate of 1569 µmol h −1 cm −2 , and extends to the efficient synthesis of five additional amino acids. In a membrane‐electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer, the catalyst sustains stable operation for over 1000 h with a cumulative glycine production exceeding 1 mol. This work achieves one of the best overall performances reported to date and provides practical design guidance for the industrially relevant electrosynthesis of α‐amino acids.

title: Gradient‐Engineered Hole‐Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin–Lead and All‐Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole‐selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three‐dimensional charge‐collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular‐gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic‐cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic‐acid self‐assembled monolayer, [2‐(7H‐dibenzo[c,e]carbazol‐7‐yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom‐to‐surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole‐transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn–Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single‐junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two‐terminal all‐perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular‐gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution‐processed optoelectronic devices.

title: Multiscale Engineering of Three‐Phase Interfaces for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) offer high efficiency and zero‐emission operation, yet membrane electrode assembly performance is constrained by coupled oxygen, proton, electron, and water transport. This review summarizes advances in multiscale three‐phase interface engineering. At the nanoscale, catalyst protection, catalyst–ionomer interactions, molecular modifiers, and ionomer design improve active site accessibility and oxygen transport. At the electrode scale, support microenvironments and catalyst layer architectures regulate pore connectivity, wettability, ionomer distribution, electronic conduction, and water removal. At the device scale, structured assemblies, membranes, gas diffusion layers, microporous layers, and flow fields coordinate mass and charge transport under practical conditions. Future priorities include scalable fabrication, operando diagnostics, multiscale modeling, and AI‐assisted optimization. By integrating interfacial, electrode, and device engineering, this review provides a framework for developing durable, high‐power, low‐platinum PEMFCs and advancing automotive fuel cell stacks with improved performance, lifetime, and economic feasibility.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Band‐filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid‐band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π‐conjugated electron‐donating molecules are covalently linked to form one‐dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well‐defined amount of electron‐accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band‐filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host–guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band‐filling engineering.

title: Introducing Controlled Backbone Porosity and Functionality into Aerogels through Mesoporous Nanoparticle Assembly
abstract: Abstract Precise control over the structural architecture of aerogels remains a central challenge, particularly in integrating well-defined nanoscale porosity within the aerogel backbone. Here, we present a nanoparticle-assembly strategy for synthesizing aerogels with controlled backbone porosity using preformed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as building blocks. This approach decouples network formation from pore generation, enabling independent control over composition, structure, and porosity. The resulting MSNs aerogel exhibits a high specific surface area of 960 m2 g–1 and significantly enhanced adsorption performance compared with the corresponding powders, driven by improved accessibility of active sites within the hierarchical porous framework. The intrinsic surface roughness of the MSNs promotes interparticle interlocking, resulting in accelerated gelation, a lower percolation threshold, and enhanced structural stability during wetting, as supported by experiments and computational modeling. To demonstrate the versatility of this concept for sensing applications, a pH-responsive probe was incorporated into the MSN dispersion prior to assembly, yielding a solid-state pH indicator. These findings highlight the potential of nanoparticle assembly as a strategy for integrating controlled backbone porosity and tailored functionality into aerogels for applications in adsorption and sensing.

title: Elusive *CH–*CHO Coupling Pathway for High-Performance CO2 Electroreduction to n-Propanol
abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to high-value n-propanol represents a promising yet challenging route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, its practical implementation is severely hindered by low selectivity and activity, primarily originating from the high energy barrier involved in the rate-limiting *C2–*C1 coupling step. Herein, we have successfully constructed an elusive *CH–*CHO coupling pathway on a stable Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst, enabling low-barrier *C2 intermediate formation and highly selective n-propanol production. Leveraging the strong electron-accepting capacity of Cu2+ sites, key *CHO intermediates are strongly adsorbed and driven toward deep reduction to *CH species, effectively overcoming the critical five-electron transfer bottleneck for *CH generation. Meanwhile, adjacent Cu0 sites provide moderate and balanced adsorption of *CHO intermediates, allowing their asymmetric coupling with the Cu2+-stabilized *CH via a markedly low energy barrier, synergistically steering the reaction along the favorable *CH–*CHO pathway. In situ fiber-optic guided ATR-FTIR spectroscopy provides evidence for the coexistence of *CHO and *CHx-related intermediates, while DFT calculations further support the proposed *CH–*CHO coupling pathway. Accordingly, the Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst achieves a high n-propanol Faradaic efficiency of 18.1% at a partial current density of 72.4 mA cm–2, alongside remarkable stability. This work establishes the *CH–*CHO pathway as a powerful strategy for kinetically favorable C–C coupling, opening a new mechanistic avenue for efficient conversion of CO2 to multicarbon via electrosynthesis.

title: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical synthesis of urea from the co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate is limited by the sluggish C–N coupling process. On Cu surfaces, adsorbed CO (*CO), a species produced from CO2 reduction, is widely accepted as the key carbonaceous intermediate for C–N bond formation. However, a molecular-level understanding of how *CO participates in this process has not been fully obtained. Herein, we combine surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the C–N coupling process on polycrystalline Cu surfaces. The *CO coverage is systematically modulated by varying the nitrate concentration and CO2/CO atmosphere and correlated with the urea synthesis performance. In contrast to the previously proposed mechanism, we reveal that (1) *CO is neither the only nor the most favorable carbonaceous intermediate for urea generation. Depending on the exposed facet of Cu, C–N coupling involving the adsorbed COOH (*COOH) or CO2 (*CO2) with NO2 (*NO2) exhibits a lower kinetic barrier; (2) excessive surface coverage of *CO is detrimental to nitrate reduction and C–N coupling by blocking the active site. This work supplements a more comprehensive picture of the C–N coupling process in the electrochemical synthesis of urea and provides guidelines for the design of Cu-based electrocatalysts.

title: Supramolecular Hexaphyrin Cage: Cooperative Guest Binding and Reversible Aromaticity Switching by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly of a rigidified, antiaromatic β,β’-linked hexaphyrin ligand (1) bearing three meso-pyridyl donors with a trans-platinum(II) diacceptor corner (2) affords a discrete trigonal-prismatic metal–organic cage, CHP, in which two cofacial hexaphyrin decks are held rigidly apart by three Pt(II)-based coordination bridges. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, high-resolution ESI-MS, and DOSY establish the assembly as a single, highly symmetric [2 + 3] species, with a solution-state hydrodynamic radius consistent with the DFT-optimized geometry. Electrochemical and spectroelectrochemical studies reveal that CHP undergoes a reversible proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process, interconverting between a 24π-antiaromatic and a 26π-aromatic Hückel state upon combined treatment with a proton source and a mild chemical or electrochemical reductant, demonstrating that the switching behavior of the parent hexaphyrin is preserved within the confined 3D architecture. Furthermore, the electron-poor internal cavity of CHP encapsulates two planar zinc(II) porphyrazine guests in a discrete 1:2 host–guest complex with positive cooperativity, as quantified by UV–vis titration. This work establishes a strategy for embedding the electronic responsiveness of expanded porphyrinoids within discrete, functional supramolecular hosts.

title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
abstract: ABSTRACT Arene‐perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, as a representative class of π‐hole‐driven noncovalent interactions, have demonstrated unique advantages in molecular recognition and supramolecular assembly. However, the precise regulation of hydrophobic aromatic molecules in aqueous environments through AP interactions remains challenging. Herein, we designed and constructed a series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self‐assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end‐group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These perfluoroarene amphiphiles readily formed stable lamellar vesicular assemblies in aqueous solution. The π‐hole region of the perfluoroarene moiety interacted with PAHs through AP interactions, facilitating the incorporation of guest molecules into the confined lamellar domains. Consequently, a variety of hydrophobic PAHs were successfully encapsulated in aqueous media, accompanied by effective modulation of their excited‐state behaviors. Moreover, the chiral confined microenvironment induced chiroptical responses from achiral PAHs, enabling efficient chirality transfer. This work provides a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on AP interactions.

title: Confinement Enables Direct Electrosynthesis of Acetaldoxime From CO and Nitrate
abstract: ABSTRACT Aldoximes are vital feedstocks in the fields of medicine, agriculture, and industry, yet their conventional synthesis suffers from high environmental costs and carbon footprints. Here, we report a direct electrocatalytic route to acetaldoxime via CO and NO 3 − co‐reduction. The C–N coupling efficiency in this process hinges on the kinetic match between CO reduction and NO 3 − reduction. Acetaldoxime synthesis exemplifies this challenge: sluggish C–C dimerization contrasts with rapid NO 3 − RR, leading to over‐reduction of nitrogen species to NH 3 . We hypothesized that a confinement strategy could selectively promote C–C dimerization and enrich acetaldehyde intermediate, thereby facilitating oximation. Ultrasmall Cu nanoparticles were encapsulated within SBA‐15 mesopores to selectively accelerate the dimerization step. Combined operando Raman and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal that the confined Cu lowers the overpotential for the key C 2 intermediate to align with that for NH 2 OH generation, enabling efficient C–N coupling to acetaldoxime. The optimized Cu@SBA‐15 catalyst achieves an acetaldoxime production rate of 255.1 mmol g cat. − 1 h − 1 (partial current density: 24.6 mA cm − 2 ). This work establishes a sustainable pathway toward aldoximes, aligning with green chemistry principles while expanding the toolbox for electrocatalytic C–N bond formation.

title: Durable Superhydrophobic Surface Engineering for Agricultural and Food-Contact Systems
abstract: Agricultural machinery, storage silos, food-processing pipelines, and packaging substrates operate under harsh coupled mechanical, tribological, chemical, electrochemical, and biological stressors that bare metallic or polymeric bulk materials cannot withstand alone. Engineered superhydrophobic surface–substrate systems—combining controlled micro-/nanoscale topography with low-surface-energy chemistry to sustain a Cassie–Baxter air plastron (static water contact angle θs > 150°, sliding angle α < 10°)—impart emergent wear resistance, corrosion protection, drag reduction, and multi-foulant repulsion across pre-harvest and post-harvest environments. This review examines contemporary surface engineering advances (predominantly 2023–2026) through a process–structure–property lens. Subtractive monolithic texturing (nanosecond/femtosecond laser processing, reactive-ion etching, interference lithography) is critically compared against additive and hybrid deposition routes (nanodiamond composites, sol–gel/mesoporous silica, electrodeposition, electrospinning, cellular armor, and fluorine-free bio-dispersions). Tribological soil/mud anti-adhesion on tillage and harvesting components, electrochemical impedance corrosion protection on magnesium, aluminum, galvanized, and stainless alloys, and turbulent slip hydraulics are evaluated alongside a quantitative cross-study benchmark of bacterial log10 reductions (0.7 to 6.5 log_{10}) separating passive anticontact ceilings from dual-functional synergy. Finally, multiscale surface characterisation, non-destructive examination (plastron tracking, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, X-ray computed tomography), and quality-control protocols for PFAS-free food-contact compliance are established.

title: Conductive Coatings on Electrospun Nanofibers for Wearable Sensors: Materials, Processing, and Reliability
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrospun nanofibers provide highly porous, lightweight, and mechanically compliant architectures that are increasingly explored for wearable sensing and smart textile systems. However, most electrospun polymer nanofibers are electrically insulating, and imparting conductivity without sacrificing their porosity, mechanical compliance, or durability under real‐use conditions remains a key challenge for practical deployment. This review examines how conductive coatings can transform electrospun fiber networks into robust sensing platforms while preserving their breathable, textile‐like structure. We organize the field around three interconnected design dimensions: the fibrous matrix, the conductive phase, and the coating or assembly strategy that governs interfacial interactions and charge transport. By linking coating chemistry and microstructure to percolation behavior, electromechanical response, and structural stability, we highlight emerging strategies for creating strain‐tolerant, pore‐preserving conductive networks. Particular attention is given to reliability under cyclic deformation, environmental exposure, and laundering, which remain critical barriers to real‐world applications. Finally, we outline key materials design principles and benchmarking approaches needed to translate electrospun fiber sensors from laboratory demonstrations toward scalable smart textile technologies.

title: Spontaneous Emulsification of Long‐Chain Alkanes to Form Oil‐in‐Water Nano‐Emulsions
abstract: ABSTRACT Spontaneous emulsification (SE) of long‐chain alkanes (LCA) to form oil‐in‐water (O/W) emulsion (SE‐O/W‐LCA) holds significant promise for applications such as oil sands extraction. However, SE‐O/W‐LCA remains a long‐standing challenge due to the extremely low polarity of LCA and high oil‐water interfacial tension. Herein, we present a successful strategy for achieving SE‐O/W‐LCA based on the design of surfactant molecular architecture. Systematic studies on structure–activity relationship correlating the structure of surfactant molecular segments with SE performance lead to an optimized surfactant architecture that achieves an emulsification capacity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional surfactants. A general design guideline of surfactants is established, requiring both high LCA solubility and large hydrophilic–lipophilic balance (HLB) values for efficient SE. Fundamentally, the integrated SE mechanism, involving reverse‐micelle diffusion, Marangoni‐flow and O/W droplet formation, is elucidated alongside the corresponding thermodynamic basis and kinetic evolution. Finally, the developed strategy is successfully applied to practical oil sands extraction that delivers state‐of‐the‐art oil‐solid separation performance as compared with previously reported methods. The proposed SE‐O/W‐LCA strategy, together with the understanding of surfactant design guidelines and underlying mechanisms, is anticipated to inspire future research on low‐energy emulsification and advance the widespread industrial deployment of SE technology.

title: Biomass-enabled metal−organic framework-based macroarchitectural materials with advanced applications
abstract: Purpose The rising global demand for energy, together with the environmental pressures linked to industrial growth, has made sustainable green development a global priority. This review focuses on biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures as an important class of sustainable porous materials. Design/methodology/approach This review focuses on three main aspects: fabrication strategies, structure–property relationships (dimensions) and advanced applications. It covers key synthesis routes such as templating, interfacial assembly and reaction confinement, while showing how biomass components such as cellulose, lignin and chitosan influence material formation and performance. The review also explains how pore hierarchy, interface design, surface chemistry, transport pathways and mechanical stability determine the final properties of these systems. Findings By combining the tuneable structure and functionality of MOFs with the renewability, hierarchical architecture and easy processability of biomass, these materials address major drawbacks of conventional MOF powders, especially poor shape control, weak mechanical strength, limited mass transfer and difficult device integration. Their growing applications in adsorption, catalysis, environmental cleanup, energy storage and drug delivery are highlighted. Current challenges include large-scale production, interface control, durability and limited mechanistic understanding. Originality/value The article points to future directions for designing application-oriented biomass-enabled MOF macroarchitectures. These materials are expected to become a key platform for scalable and high-performance next-generation technologies.

title: Chiral Bobbers in the Room‐Temperature Magnet Co 8 Zn 10 Mn 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that emerge near surfaces of chiral magnets with bulk‐type Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. They can be regarded as skyrmion strings terminated by a Bloch point inside the material. So far, chiral bobbers have been observed only at cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the direct observation of chiral bobbers in over a broad temperature range, including room temperature. Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations, we identify a previously unreported nucleation pathway in which skyrmion strings transform into chiral bobbers under an applied magnetic field. We also demonstrate that chiral bobbers on opposite surfaces can be coupled to form double‐bobber states. These findings establish chiral bobbers as room‐temperature magnetic textures and identify their role in the nucleation pathways of topological magnetic solitons.

title: Hydrothermal Synthesis of Porous MoS2 Nanosheets for Aqueous Electrochemical Capacitors
abstract: Porous MoS2 nanosheets were synthesized by a hydrothermal method and investigated as electrode materials for aqueous supercapacitors. X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of crystalline hexagonal MoS2 with an average crystallite size of approximately 3.12 nm. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a three-dimensional marigold-like assembly of interlinked nanosheets. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption measurements indicated a mesoporous textural structure, with a BET surface area of 4.6962 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.03011 cm3 g-1, and average pore width of approximately 25.8 nm. The high-relative-pressure hysteresis is consistent with interparticle voids within the nanosheet assembly. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirmed the presence of Mo and S, with no impurity-related elemental signals detected within the measurement sensitivity. Electrochemical performance was evaluated in 1 M KOH using a three-electrode system. Cyclic voltammetry showed Faradaic charge-storage behavior and delivered a specific capacitance of 165.17 F g-1 at a scan rate of 10 mV s-1. Galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements yielded a specific capacitance of 110.66 F g-1 at 1 A g-1, corresponding to estimated electrode-level gravimetric energy and power densities of 7.53 Wh kg-1 and 349.95 W kg-1, respectively. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed electrolyte and charge-transfer resistances of 4.75 and 1.77 Ω, respectively, indicating favorable ion transport and charge-transfer kinetics. Kinetic analysis indicated a mixed charge-storage mechanism dominated by diffusion-controlled processes, with a smaller surface-controlled contribution. The mesoporous nanosheet assembly, together with the observed electrochemical performance, demonstrates the potential of hydrothermally prepared MoS2 as an electrode material for aqueous supercapacitors.

title: Injectable Self‐Healing Microspheres Enable In Situ Assembly of Dynamic Porous Scaffolds for Tissue Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Tissue engineering scaffolds are indispensable for repairing complex tissue defects; however, conventional prefabricated scaffolds are limited by invasive implantation, poor anatomical conformity, and insufficient adaptability to irregular defect geometries. Here, we report an injectable, self‐assembling scaffold strategy that transforms polymer microspheres from isolated functional carriers into dynamic modular building blocks for in situ scaffold construction. Following injection, the self‐healing microspheres fill irregular defects, fuse with adjacent microspheres, and form a mechanically stable three‐dimensional scaffold with an interconnected porous architecture. This design combines the minimally invasive delivery and functional versatility of microspheres with the structural integrity and mechanical support of macroscopic scaffolds, thereby addressing a key challenge in precise and conformal tissue repair. The platform also enables disease‐specific functionalization through metal‐ion coordination. Silver‐ion‐loaded microspheres provide conformal coverage of complex wounds while exhibiting antibacterial activity and supporting skin regeneration. Zinc‐ion‐functionalized microspheres assemble into defect‐matched porous scaffolds and promote osteogenic repair. Copper‐ion‐integrated microspheres remain localized at tumor sites and provide sustained release of therapeutic agents, thereby reducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work establishes a minimally invasive, shape‐adaptive, and customizable scaffold platform for complex tissue repair and localized therapy. More broadly, it provides a versatile design framework for the development of next‐generation intelligent biomaterials.

title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH &gt; 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS) 2 CrO 4 , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm 3 g −1 of Ne but only 0.40 cm 3 g −1 of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a compelling platform for coupling photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production with organic valorization. However, the practical efficiency remains limited by rapid electron‐hole recombination. Inspired by the conformational rigidity and planar geometry imposed by peptide bonds, we develop a conformational locking strategy that introduces a fused‐ring linker, which restricts backbone rotation and thereby enhances framework planarity and conjugation, affording a series of COFs (TFPPy‐DATMBP, TFPPy‐DABP, and TFPPy‐DAPy) with progressively improved planarity and conjugation. The conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy achieves an impressive H 2 O 2 production rate of 119.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , with an apparent quantum yield up to 29.14% at 410 nm, while delivering a yield of >98% toward the high‐value imine product. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy extends the lifetime of the long‐lived charge‐separated state by approximately 10‐fold to 102.87 ps, compared with 10.34 ps for TFPPy‐DATMBP. This work establishes TFPPy‐DAPy as an efficient photocatalyst for fine chemical co‐production, and provides a generalizable molecular‐level design strategy for developing advanced catalysts across diverse photocatalytic applications.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
abstract: Abstract Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

title: Highly Crystalline Triptycene-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Achieving high crystallinity in three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly beyond 4-connected tetrahedral nodes toward higher-connectivity building units. Here, we report the rapid synthesis of three highly crystalline triptycene-based COFs (COF-563, −564, and −565) as well-faceted, micrometer-sized crystals under mild conditions within 24 h. By employing rigid 6-connected trigonal prismatic triptycene-based building units, hexakis(4-aminophenyl/4-formylphenyl)triptycene (Trip-NH2/Trip-CHO), we access a topological regime of three-dimensional (3D) COFs that includes the established hea and stp nets as well as an unprecedented (6,6)-connected htp topology. These frameworks are constructed through reticulation of the triptycene nodes with tetrahedral (tetra(4-anilyl)methane (TAM)), rectangular (pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetraaniline (PyTTA)), and hexagonal (hexakis(4′-formyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)benzene (HFBB)) complementary linkers to yield the hea, stp, and htp structures, respectively. The resulting materials exhibit permanent porosity with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface areas of up to 3769 m2 g–1─approaching a 2-fold increase over previously reported values for related topologies─and thermal stability up to 500 °C. This work establishes a versatile platform for the rapid formation of highly crystalline 3D organic frameworks and provides a blueprint for designing complex, highly porous architectures with controlled topology.

title: Solvent‐Induced Reversible Phase Transition in Microporous Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks for Molecular‐Sieving Separation of CO 2 and C 2 H 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient separation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) remains a critical challenge in the chemical industry for C 2 H 2 purification, due to their highly similar molecular sizes and physicochemical property. Here we report a HOF material, denoted HIAM‐105, assembled from a tetracarboxylic acid building block. It undergoes reversible structural transformation upon solvent removal and inclusion. The guest‐free structure (HIAM‐105a) features precisely matched pore dimensions with CO 2 molecules while fully excluding C 2 H 2 , enabling molecular sieving separation of CO 2 /C 2 H 2 . At 298 K and 1 bar, HIAM‐105a achieves a CO 2 adsorption capacity of 44.0 cm 3 g −1 , resulting in a CO 2 /C 2 H 2 adsorption capacity ratio as high as 23.9, which outperforms most previously reported sieving adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm that HIAM‐105a can produce C 2 H 2 with ultrahigh purity from CO 2 /C 2 H 2 mixtures, and more importantly, it can be readily regenerated through gas purging at ambient conditions.

title: Synergistic Coordination and Crosslinking Strategy for Scalable, Self‐Repairable C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 Separation Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene/ethane (C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 ) separation is one of the most energy‐intensive processes in the chemical industry, and membrane technology offers a promising low‐energy alternative. However, conventional mixed‐matrix membranes (MMMs) suffer from poor filler dispersion and interfacial defects, especially at high MOF loadings. Here we report a synergistic coordination and crosslinking strategy to fabricate highly compatible, high‐loaded UTSA‐280‐integrated hydrogel MMMs for efficient C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 separation. By exploiting the dual role of calcium ions (Ca 2+ ), which simultaneously coordinate with squaric acid to grow UTSA‐280 and crosslink sodium alginate (SA) chains, we achieve in situ growth of uniformly dispersed UTSA‐280 nanoparticles (mean size 4.32 nm) within a semisolid hydrogel network. The resulting membrane exhibits a high MOF loading of 27.39 wt%, a C 2 H 4 /C 2 H 6 mixture separation factor of 4.0 at 7 bar, and stable operation for over 1780 h. The hydrogel matrix also confers a remarkable self‐repair capability, fully restoring separation performance after mechanical damage. Moreover, a 200 cm 2 large‐area membrane was readily fabricated, demonstrating a cost‐effective route to scalable ethylene purification.

title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal‐Shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn‐Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO 2 Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon‐capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn‐triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared‐layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2 + cations, 1,2,4‐triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3‐dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane‐1,3‐dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid‐assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal‐shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO 2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW‐DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO 2 ‐loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest‐responsive flexibility of the Zn‐Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO 2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C─H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO 2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selectivity for CO 2 over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal‐shaped core as powerful pore‐controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO 2 capture under operative conditions.

title: The Chemistry and Applications of High-Connectivity Metal–Organic Frameworks: From Carboxylate-Based to Benzotriazolate-Based Platforms
abstract: Conspectus Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), assembled from inorganic nodes and organic linkers via strong coordination bonds, are functional crystalline porous materials. Reticular chemistry can guide the assembly of targeted MOFs from preselected building blocks encoding the geometrical information on underlying networks. Among them, high-connectivity nets are important for the designed synthesis of high-connectivity MOF materials, assembled from associated building blocks, thanks to their high structural predictability. These building blocks can be polytopic organic ligands, polynuclear clusters and metal–organic polyhedra, and their geometrical shapes and connectivities often precisely match the targeted high-connectivity nets. High-connectivity carboxylate-based MOFs often display high porosity and are promising adsorbents for gases while benzotriazolate-based MOFs are emerging as a distinctive subclass of MOFs constructed by robust metal–nitrogen bonds, which can stabilize reactive species such as low-valent metal centers, therefore enhancing guest-framework interactions. To this end, it remains a challenge to rationally assemble high-connectivity building blocks into carboxylate- and benzotriazolate-based MOFs with tailored pore structures and functionalities for advanced applications. In this Account, we summarized recent progress from our group toward the synthesis and applications of high-connectivity MOFs, ranging from carboxylate-based to benzotriazolate-based platforms. We first introduced π-extended PrismCage building units into isoreticular (6,6)-connected nia-MOFs for enhanced supramolecular host–guest interactions. Next, we established a net-coded organic building block strategy to rationally construct (4,12)-connected shp-MOFs and (6,12)-connected alb-MOFs via the assembly of a 12-connected hexagonal-prismatic dodecacarboxylate ligand and geometrically different inorganic nodes. Next, we further developed a heterosupermolecular-building-block approach to assemble trinodal (3,12,24)-connected uru-MOFs by assembling 12-connected cuboctahedral and 24-connected rhombicuboctahedral metal–organic polyhedra, which are linked by 3-connected organic units. The high-porosity uru-MOF-1 exhibits good low-temperature methane storage performances. We also applied a multicomponent merged-net strategy to precisely synthesize (3,6,9)-connected tsn-MOF-1 by assembling 9-connected metal-containing trinuclear clusters, 6-connected triptycene-based carboxylates, and 3-connected pyridine-based linkers. The robust tsn-MOF-1 can facilely be activated from common solvents to achieve full porosity, exhibiting good methane and hydrogen storage performances. Apart from carboxylate-based MOF platforms, we constructed functional benzotriazolate-based MOFs using multitopic benzotriazolate ligands synthesized via sequential reactions including general Suzuki coupling reactions. We first synthesized a tritopic benzotriazolate ligand and assembled it with copper ions to form a rod-packing MOF with high ionic conductivity. Furthermore, the assembly of a hexatopic benzotriazolate ligand and Zn5 clusters forms a (6,6)-connected nia-MOF, Zn-Tz6Mes. The isostructural CuI-Zn-Tz6Mes with open Cu(I) sites exhibits enhanced binding affinities toward π-acidic gases such as H2 and N2 compared to the parent Zn-Tz6Mes. The serendipitous assembly of a tritopic tris-benzotriazolate ligand and zinc ions afford a (3,6,6)-connected pco-MOF, Zn-TBTB, displaying a complex cage-within-cage structure and modular anionic pore environments for high Li+ conductivity. Finally, we give a brief perspective toward high-connectivity functional MOFs and hope this Account can serve as a guiding blueprint for the development of next-generation high-connectivity MOFs with embedded functionalities, thereby advancing the field of the solid-state materials in general.

title: Guest-Modulated Pyrene-Based Metal–Organic Framework toward Enhanced Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient photocatalysts for solar-driven H2 production remains a challenge in sustainable energy research. Herein, we report a guest-modulated strategy to construct a high-performance photocatalyst by encapsulating a cationic dye, (4-dimethylaminostyryl)-1-methylpyridine (DMASM), into an anionic pyrene-based metal–organic framework (MOF), Zn-Py ([BMI]3[Na3Zn3(TBAPy)3], H4TBAPy = 1,3,6,8-tetrakis(p-benzoic acid)pyrene), synthesized via ionic liquid-directed assembly. The resulting host–guest system, DMASM@Zn-Py, exhibits a narrowed bandgap from 2.39 to 2.02 eV, significantly extending visible-light absorption. Spectroscopic investigations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal efficient energy transfer from the TBAPy ligand to the DMASM guest, accompanied by spatial separation of the highest occupied crystal orbital (HOCO) and lowest unoccupied crystal orbital (LUCO) on the framework and dye, respectively. This spatial separation effectively suppresses photogenerated electron–hole recombination, as evidenced by about a 5.6-fold enhancement in photocurrent density and a substantially reduced charge-transfer resistance. Remarkably, DMASM@Zn-Py achieves a cocatalyst-free photocatalytic H2 evolution rate of 1065.5 μmol·g–1·h–1, far surpassing that of pristine Zn-Py (225.69 μmol·g–1·h–1). This work establishes a clear molecular engineering paradigm for designing efficient MOF-based photocatalysts through tunable host–guest interactions.

title: Bioinspired Plasma‐Programmed Supramolecular Interfaces for Proton Relay‐Driven Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
abstract: Solar‐driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production is fundamentally constrained by inefficient proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET); asynchronous proton delivery and electron transport impede formation of key oxygenated intermediates. Herein, we report a plasma‐programmed supramolecular proton‐relay interface COF (SPRI‐COF) for H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Inspired by cytochrome c oxidase, SPRI‐COF harnesses plasma‐programmed hydrogen bonding carbon dots (HB‐CDs) within a surface‐programmed COF (SP‐COF). Incorporating HB‐CDs transforms the parent SP‐COF framework into a hydrogen bond‐directed supramolecular composite, SPRI‐COF, wherein an interconnected proton‐relay network composed of complementary hydrogen bonds and confined water molecules is established. SPRI‐COF reveals a hydrogen bond‐rich interfacial microenvironment that facilitates proton‐coupled oxygen conversion while maintaining favorable charge‐carrier dynamics. Benefiting from interfacial polarization, altered carrier dynamics, and the hydrogen bond‐rich interfacial environment, SPRI‐COF achieves an H 2 O 2 production rate of 2387 µmol g − 1 h − 1 , approximately 4.5 times that of SP‐COF, together with improved selectivity toward the two‐electron oxygen reduction pathway. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analyses, and theoretical calculations collectively support the cooperative contributions of interfacial electronic regulation, hydrogen bond‐mediated proton transfer, and *OOH (* = adsorbed) stabilization to the enhanced photocatalytic performance. This work demonstrates a plasma‐enabled supramolecular strategy for integrating local proton‐transfer regulation with interfacial electronic modulation in photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production.

title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
abstract: Abstract Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.

title: Reconstructing Structural Dynamic Cooperativity Suppresses Conduction Loss in Linear Aliphatic Polymer Dielectrics at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with different π‐electron delocalization affect structural dynamic cooperativity and charge transport. Side‐group modification alters intermolecular interactions and local dynamic constraints, shifting long‐range cooperative motion to localized heterogeneous fluctuations. This transition coincides with reduced collective structural fluctuations and improved local electronic‐state stability, consistent with suppressed phonon‐assisted carrier transport. As a result, the furan‐modified polymer exhibits a statistical electronic energy fluctuation descriptor of 0.132 eV and nearly two orders of magnitude higher volume resistivity. It achieves a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm −3 at 120°C, approximately 45 times that of pristine polymer while maintaining a charge‐discharge efficiency above 90%. It also retains an efficiency above 93% over 5 × 10 5 charge‐discharge cycles at 200 MV m −1 . Although the higher glass transition temperature of the furan‐modified polymer may also contribute to its performance near 120°C, its advantage is already evident at 25°C and 80°C, well below the glass‐transition regime. This work highlights structural dynamic cooperativity as a descriptor linking molecular dynamics and charge transport in linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics.

title: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
abstract: Abstract Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.

title: Metal–Backboned Architectures Enable Magneto–Spin–Charge Engineering for High–Performance Li–CO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneous CO 2 conversion and high–energy–density energy storage are urgently needed for sustainable energy systems where Li–CO 2 batteries provide an ideal solution, yet their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish CO 2 redox kinetics. Emerging metal–backboned molecules, which contain numerous metal atoms as catalytically active sites, are expected to accelerate CO 2 reduction reaction kinetics due to their unique architectures and properties. Herein, we report a novel mixed–valence cobalt–backboned polymer with effective spin manipulation as an efficient electrocatalyst and conductive scaffold for Li–CO 2 batteries, which enables a low overpotential of 1.06 V and outstanding stable cycling over 2700 h. An external magnetic field drives Co centers from low–spin to high–spin configuration and enhances intermetallic intervalence charge transfer, synergistically strengthening CO 2 adsorption and activation by increasing unpaired electron orbital occupancy and facilitating electron transfer to CO 2 antibonding orbitals. This work establishes metal–backboned architectures as a versatile platform for spin–charge cooperative engineering, opening a new avenue for kinetically accelerated next–generation energy storage systems.

title: Fully π‐Conjugated Nonvolatile n‐Type Additives Toward 21% Efficiency in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid additive engineering represents a key strategy to modulate the morphology of organic solar cells via intermolecular interactions (van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, and dipole interaction) with photoactive materials. However, these weak interactions lack sufficient capacity to control the crystallization and phase separation of active layer. Here, we developed a conjugated electrostatic coupling strategy to strengthen the intermolecular forces between solid additives and donor/acceptor. The solid additive we designed possesses a fully conjugated structure that can generate strong electrostatic potential interaction, therefore a small amount of solid additive (3 wt%) facilitate ordered crystalline fibril growth of polymer donor and dense molecular packing of acceptor. In addition, the n‐type nature and nonvolatile feature of solid additive promotes the electron transport capacity and stability of the active layer. As a result, the optimal device achieved a state‐of‐the‐art efficiency of 21.02% (certificated to 20.55%), due to the prolonged exciton lifetime, suppressed charge recombination, and enhanced charge collection efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for solid additive engineering in organic photovoltaics.

title: Dual‐Asymmetric Giant Molecule Acceptors Featuring Asymmetric Terminals and Flexible Alkyl‐Flank Architecture for Efficient and Robust Non‐Halogen Solvent‐Processed Binary and Ternary Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible‐linked giant‐molecule acceptors (F‐GMAs) suffer from inferior intermolecular packing, limiting their efficiency in non‐halogenated processed binary organic solar cells (OSCs). Moreover, asymmetric‐terminal‐based regioregular F‐GMAs remain challenging. Here, we propose a dual‐asymmetric‐rigid‐within‐flexible molecular strategy and synthesize four flanking linker‐based F‐GMAs ( DY4T‐F , DY8T‐F , DY12T‐F , dual‐asymmetric ADY8T‐FCl ) by progressively lengthening the alkyl linker and symmetric/asymmetric terminals, alongside a dual‐asymmetric monomeric AY4T‐FCl . The AY4T‐FCl crystal exhibited diverse intermolecular packing modes and efficient charge transport channels due to the synergistic outer thienyl flanking chain and asymmetric terminals. ADY8T‐FCl exhibits stronger intramolecular folding, enhanced crystallinity, and higher electron mobility than other neat films. o ‐XY: CS 2 ‐processed D18 : ADY8T‐FCl ‐based as‐cast binary OSCs yield a remarkable PCE of 20.35% with a low nonradiative recombination energy loss (Δ E 3 ) of 0.183 eV, setting benchmarks for all‐F‐GMA‐based and non‐halogenated‐solvent‐processed binary OSCs. Notably, D18 : ADY8T‐FCl flexible binary OSCs achieve an outstanding PCE of 18.41%, significantly better than other counterparts. More interestingly, D18 : L8‐BO‐X : ADY8T‐FCl ‐based devices achieve a champion PCE of 20.82% among F‐GMAs‐based ternary OSCs. Our work demonstrates that the dual‐asymmetric‐rigid‐within‐flexible strategy for flank‐connected F‐GMAs with alkyl‐length engineering and asymmetric terminals offers a promising pathway for concurrently achieving record efficiency, ultralow Δ E 3 , and superior mechanical robustness in non‐halogenated processed flexible/rigid binary and rigid ternary OSCs.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Phenazine‐based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one‐step two‐electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π – π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2′‐(phenazine‐2,3‐diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot‐scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large‐scale energy storage applications.

title: Multifunctional Mesoporous Bioactive Glass Nanoparticles Promote Osteogenesis via Immunomodulation
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) is a promising biomaterial for bone-defect repair. However, MBG lacks an immunomodulatory capability, which is vital for effective bone regeneration, thus limiting its clinical application. Herein, MBG grafted with mannose (MBG-g-Man) was designed to target and interact with macrophages via the recognition of the mannose receptor (CD206) and promote M2 polarization. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MBG-g-Man exhibits excellent biocompatibility, precise macrophage targeting, and efficient cellular uptake while also recruiting and polarizing macrophages toward the M2 phenotype. Furthermore, osteogenic differentiation assays revealed that the ALP activity of MBG-g-Man was 157.89 units/L, which is much higher than that of MBG (127.85 units/L), demonstrating that MBG-g-Man may be an effective bone regeneration material. This research may provide a promising strategy for designing functional biomaterials for bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

title: Matcha-Assisted Synthesis of a NiCo2O4−ZnO-rGO Ternary Nanoarchitecture for Nanomolar Level Electrochemical Dopamine Detection
abstract: Abstract Developing cost-effective, environmentally benign and highly sensitive electrocatalysts for neurochemical sensing remains a crucial goal in bioanalytical chemistry. Herein, we report a green, hydrothermal strategy for synthesizing a NiCo2O4−ZnO-reduced graphene oxide (rGO) ternary nanoarchitecture using matcha green tea extract as a multifunctional stabilizing and reducing agent. The bioactive phytochemicals in matcha mediated the simultaneous nucleation of redox-active NiCo2O4, ZnO nanoparticles alongside the partial reduction of graphene oxide, forming an interconnected conductive network without toxic chemical reductants. Structural and morphological characterizations confirmed the successful integration of all three functional phases. Electrochemical assessments via cyclic voltammetry (CV) revealed that the NiCo2O4−ZnO-rGO exhibited the highest oxidation peak current of 6.24 μA, compared with 1.13 μA for bare GCE and around 3−5 μA for individual and binary modified electrodes, displaying a superior electrocatalytic oxidation current for dopamine (DA) driven by synergistic charge transfer between the multi-valence transition metals and the highly conductive rGO framework. Chronoamperometric analysis demonstrated a broad working range of 0.02−300 μM, comprising three linear regions of 0.02−0.10, 0.20−8, and 10−300 μM. The low-concentration region exhibited the highest sensitivity of 8.409 μA cm-2 μM-1 with an LOD of 8.9 nM. CV calibration showed two linear regions of 2−8 and 10−100 μM, with an LOD of 71 nM determined from the low-concentration region. Furthermore, the sensor demonstrates excellent anti-interference capabilities in the simultaneous presence of uric acid, ascorbic acid and glucose, alongside robust reproducibility, repeatability and operational stability. This work establishes a sustainable, facile synthesis route for high-performance non-precious nanomaterials in clinical and neurochemical diagnostic applications.

title: Self‐Templated Catalytic Assembly Overcomes Diffusion Limits in Dynamic DNA Circuits for Sensitive Biomarker Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic DNA circuits offer programmable platforms for clinical biomarker detection, but their translation is limited by slow diffusion‐controlled kinetics and inadequate amplification of low‐abundance targets. Herein, we introduce a self‐templated catalytic assembly (SCA) circuit that overcomes diffusion limitations by converting target‐induced catalytic assembly into an amplified fluorescence signal, enabling robust and efficient detection of N‐terminal pro‐brain natriuretic peptide (NT‐proBNP), the gold‐standard biomarker for heart failure (HF). The SCA circuit employs interconnected hairpin reactants that autonomously assemble into a dynamic four‐branched DNA scaffold, which spatially concentrates probes and converts diffusion‐limited hybridization into efficient template‐directed catalysis. This design accelerates the reaction rate constant ( k a ) by 2.61‐fold, facilitating repeated catalytic turnover and sustained signal amplification. With aptamer‐guaranteed molecular recognition and localization‐intensified signal amplification, the SCA circuit revealed improved diagnostic performance for HF patients than the clinically adopted fluorescence immunochromatography assay (FICA) in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, the self‐adaptive SCA circuit enabled accurate risk stratification of HF patients, with all samples in the investigated cohort correctly classified. Attributed to the programmability and modularity, the SCA circuit can be readily adapted for detecting trace amounts of clinically relevant biomarkers, providing a pivotal molecular toolbox for real‐time therapeutic monitoring.

title: Architecture‐Dependent Aromatic Residue Interactions Drive Optoelectronic Activity in Peptide Coassemblies
abstract: This work presents a fluorination-based peptidic strategy for orchestrating the organization of π-units within biomolecular assemblies, specifically by facilitating the co-mixing of arene/perfluoroarene units and the architecture of their presentation (symmetric vs. asymmetric) as a molecular knob for modulating bulk photophysical and optoelectronic properties. Peptide-flanked quaterthiophene (4T) and perylene diimide (PDI) serve as model energy donor-acceptor units, where donor units carry either phenylalanine (F) or pentafluorophenylalanine (F5) residues. Systematic studies on architecture-dependent presentation of aromatic residues and their pairs on 4T/PDI-bearing peptides exhibit distinct effects on the properties of the resulting optoelectronic material. Molecular dynamics simulations provide insights into probable interactions of chromophoric/peptidic units within donor-acceptor coassemblies. Together, experimental findings and simulations suggest a greater tendency for coassembly between 4T and PDI cores in the asymmetric than in the symmetric designs. Additionally, the fluorine-containing asymmetric design exhibits a higher propensity for co-alignment between 4T and PDI cores in H-like patterns within the simulations. Asymmetric F+F5 coassemblies and annealed, fluorinated symmetric coassemblies show better photocurrent generation relative to other film sample conditions. Overall, the utility of a non-canonical aromatic amino acid design offers an effective molecular engineering approach for modulating peptide-templated assembly states and bulk properties of water-processable bioelectronic systems.

title: Ambient Drying Enabled Energy Efficient Fabrication of Skin‐Free Aerogel Evaporators for High‐Performance Interfacial Solar Evaporation
abstract: Aerogel‐based evaporators are widely explored for interfacial solar evaporation (ISE), yet their fabrication generally relies on energy‐intensive freeze‐drying, creating an inherent contradiction with the sustainable nature of solar desalination. Moreover, freeze‐drying generates dense surface skin that restricts vapor escape and reduces evaporation area. Here, we report an ambient‐temperature and atmospheric‐pressure drying strategy that transforms the drying process from simple solvent removal process into structural engineering of sodium alginate (SA) aerogel evaporators. Gluconolactone‐triggered gradual Ca 2+ release enables thorough in situ crosslinking which mechanically stabilizes the gel network, while sacrificial CaCO 3 templating, CO 2 bubble evolution, and low‐surface‐tension solvent exchange preserve a skin‐free porous surface during ambient drying. Concurrently, gel domains formed within vertically oriented channels regulate water transport, establishing a balance between water supply and evaporation. The resulting aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 2.36 kg m −2 h −1 under one sun, compared with 1.84 kg m −2 h −1 for its freeze‐dried counterpart, while reducing fabrication energy consumption by 94.8% and processing time by 55.6%, and increasing tensile strength by 537%. Life‐cycle assessment reveals a 96.5% reduction in CO 2 emissions. This work establishes low‐energy drying as a means of simultaneously programming aerogel surfaces and mass transport, providing a sustainable route toward high‐performance solar evaporators.

title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
abstract: Abstract Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using d STORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

title: A Low-Rank Modeling Framework for Adsorption Isotherm Reconstruction in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive separation offers an energy-efficient alternative to distillation, yet adsorption data sets often remain incomplete due to the high cost of experiments and simulations, limiting their use in large-scale materials screening. In this work, we address the challenge of sparsity in adsorption data sets by reformulating adsorption isotherms as an incomplete material–adsorption property matrix and analyzing them using a low-rank modeling (LRM) framework. Using Ar and N2 adsorption in metal–organic frameworks as representative case studies, we demonstrate that adsorption properties across pressures and adsorbates exhibit strong and systematic correlations, revealing an inherent low-rank structure in the adsorption data. Our analysis shows that reconstruction performance depends on the latent dimension (k) and regularization strength (λ), with the optimal ranges of k and λ determined from systematic hyperparameter analysis. Comparison of different LRM variants demonstrates that latent representations are important for capturing pressure-dependent trends, with the latent-bias (LB) and latent-only (LO) models consistently providing substantially better reconstruction than the bias-only (BO) model in the considered reconstruction settings. The LRM framework captures both the qualitative shape of adsorption isotherms and the absolute magnitude of uptake across a wide range of materials and adsorption behaviors. Systematic variation of data availability shows that reconstruction accuracy improves with increasing availability of observed entries, while naturally occurring pressure-dependent missingness in the N2 data set can also be reconstructed without requiring additional simulations. Cross-adsorbate analysis further shows that Ar adsorption contains information that can be used to reconstruct N2 adsorption, while jointly available Ar–N2 data substantially improve the performance of latent models. Quantitative comparison with the Uni-MOF framework shows that the latent LRM models achieve comparable or higher R2 values at several corresponding pressure points for Ar and N2 adsorption. Overall, these results demonstrate that LRM offers a data-efficient approach for reconstructing adsorption isotherms from incomplete data sets by leveraging correlations within adsorption properties.

title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

title: Porphyrin-Phenothiazine-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Enhanced Photocatalytic Nitrogen Fixation
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven photocatalytic nitrogen reduction represents a promising and environmentally benign approach for ammonia synthesis. However, developing efficient photocatalysts capable of converting nitrogen to ammonia under ambient conditions remains a significant challenge. Porphyrin compounds exhibit excellent photosensitive properties with strong absorption across both the ultraviolet and visible regions of the solar spectrum, while phenothiazine offers unique optoelectronic activity. In this study, we integrated these two motifs and synthesized a series of novel metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) by structural modification of the phenothiazine linker with a methyl group and with oxygen-containing functional groups. All three frameworks are active for N2 photoreduction under visible light, and the activity depends systematically on the linker: the sulfone-functionalized COF-3 reaches 109.6 ± 3.6 μmol g–1 h–1 (1866.2 ± 60.7 μg h–1 gcat–1), outperforming both the unmodified (COF-1) and the methyl-modified (COF-2) frameworks. Mechanistic analysis and theoretical calculations revealed that the introduced oxygen atoms facilitate the separation and transport of photogenerated electrons within the framework. This work shows that rational molecular-level pre-design and fine-tuning of the linker can profoundly influence the structural and optoelectronic properties of COF-based photocatalysts, enabling superior activity without the need for metallic elements or co-catalysts.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO 2 /H 2 O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.
